Subject: Regional SI partnership inquiry — DE & SG residency needs

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking a look — I'm Oliver from Atlas Consulting. We're a systems integrator with a strong presence across DACH and APAC (Singapore/Taiwan). A few enterprise customers have asked us to recommend LLM inference partners that can support: 
- data residency guarantees (Germany, Singapore)
- VPC/private deployments or a dedicated-hosted model in region
- SOC2 + local certification evidence

I've attached our company profile and a zip of some compliance artifacts for context (Atlas_SI_profile.pdf, Compliance_Certificates.zip).

High-level ask: would Redwood consider a pilot where Atlas leads integration for two customers (one DE, one SG) and Redwood provides a dedicated instance or private deployment with data residency controls? We're happy to sign an NDA/MAA; both customers expect a short timeline (6–8 weeks for a POC).

If useful, I can do a 30-minute intro demo next week. Proposed times: Tue 2027-05-31 09:00-10:00 CEST or Wed 2027-06-01 10:00-11:00 SGT.

Best,
Oliver

Hi Oliver — thanks for reaching out and for the materials.

Looping in Marissa (partners) and Soojin (channel ops) to triage. High-level — Redwood supports three deployment modes that look like good fits depending on customer constraints: Hosted + region pinning, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC/on-prem). For strong residency guarantees we'd typically look at Dedicated in-region or Private with customer-managed networking.

Quick asks to help us scope the pilot:
- Are the customers asking for physical on-prem (air-gapped) or can they accept VPC/private deployment in a cloud region?
- Any KMS/HSM requirements?
- Expected throughput (rps / concurrent sessions) and typical sequence lengths (avg tokens) for the POC?
- Are there contractual templates (SLA, DPA) they expect us to sign?

Marissa / Soojin — can you triage legal/partner commercial asks and confirm if a 6–8 week pilot timeline is reasonable given engineering/SE availability? I can host the intro meeting Tue 09:00 CEST if that works.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Strategic Partners, Redwood Inference

Thanks Naomi — Oliver, great to e-meet. A few operational notes from Partner Ops: 

1) Commercial & timeline
- Pilot model: recommend a 6-week technical POC (week 1-2 setup + week 3-5 testing + week 6 validation).
- We can offer a limited pilot credit for orchestration/runtime cost; channel discounts can be discussed post-POC.

2) Deployment options (quick summary)
- Dedicated in-region: best for predictable throughput and residency (we can pin capacity to eu-west-1 for DE customers).
- Private (VPC): full control, customer-managed networking and KMS; ideal for regulated customers.

3) Contracting & security
- We'll need to share our standard DPA + SOC2 report with your customers; Legal will need their procurement contact for DPA redlines.
- For SG engagement, we should confirm data export rules; Soojin, can you flag any APAC-specific checklist items?

- Vivek: run a quick feasibility for DE + SG network/topology and confirm resource estimates (GPU types, RAM, expected latency).

Hi all,

Quick feasibility note after a first pass:
- DE (Customer A): Dedicated in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) is straightforward. We can provision reserved GPU pool (A10G-class) and pin model versions. Network: we will require a peered VPC and an ingress endpoint; TLS termination stays on customer side if they use Private. KMS: we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS; HSM integrations need a short ops window to validate.
- SG (Customer B): Singapore region is supported for Dedicated. If the customer insists on on-prem, we'll need a Private appliance (air-gapped) engagement which adds ~3 weeks to scheduling and requires an on-site engineer for initial setup.

Attachments: residency-deployment-sketch.png (sketch of VPC peering + routing for both scenarios).

Questions for Atlas / customers:
- Expected concurrent sessions and tokens per request (this drives batch size and GPU sizing).
- Any requirement for real-time streaming vs. batch inference (affects runtime decisions).

I can prep a sizing matrix once we have throughput numbers. Happy to join the intro call.

-Vivek
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

- SG customer (RetailCo, Singapore): prefers cloud-hosted in SG region; on-prem not required for pilot. Throughput: ~12 concurrent, avg 600 tokens, batch-heavy. Procurement contact: rajiv@retailco.sg
